title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 8
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 8: the generosity of the assemblies of Macedonia, the call to complete the collection, and the brothers sent with Titus.

questions.text: In which assemblies had the grace of God been given, as the writer makes known at the start of the chapter?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 makes known to them the grace of God which has been given in the assemblies of Macedonia.

answers.text: The grace given in the assemblies of Galatia
The grace given in the assemblies of Asia
The grace given in the assemblies of Macedonia
The grace given in the assembly at Jerusalem

questions.text: What does verse 2 say their deep poverty abounded to?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says that in much proof of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded to the riches of their generosity.

answers.text: To the riches of their generosity
To the growth of their numbers
To the silence of their adversaries
To the building of a temple

questions.text: What does the text say about how and how much they gave?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says that according to their power, and beyond their power, they gave of their own accord.

answers.text: They gave only what had been commanded of them
They gave after much persuasion from others
They gave less than they had promised before
They gave of their own accord, according to and beyond their power

questions.text: What did they do first, which was not as had been expected?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says this was not as we had expected, but first they gave their own selves to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.

answers.text: They first sent letters on ahead to the saints in Jerusalem
They first gave their own selves to the Lord, and to the writer and his companions
They first asked for a delay of a year in the whole matter
They first chose men to carry the gift to Jerusalem

questions.text: Whom did they urge to complete this grace in the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says they urged Titus that, as he had made a beginning before, so he would also complete in them this grace.

answers.text: Titus
Timothy
Apollos
Stephanas

questions.text: What does verse 9 say about the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that through his poverty you might become rich.

answers.text: That he was poor and remained poor to the very end
That he gave away his riches to the saints in Jerusalem
That though he was rich, he became poor for their sakes, that they might become rich
That he commanded them to give away everything they had

questions.text: According to verse 12, by what measure is the gift acceptable?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says that if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what you have, not according to what you don't have.

answers.text: According to what others in Macedonia have given
According to what they have, not according to what they do not have
According to the sum they promised a year ago
According to the amount the assemblies have set

questions.text: What reason does verse 14 give for their abundance supplying the lack of others?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says it is for equality: their abundance at this present time supplies the others' lack, so that the others' abundance may also become a supply for their lack, that there may be equality.

answers.text: So that the others may praise them
So that they may be eased and the others distressed
So that the gift may be larger than that of Macedonia
For equality, so that abundance and lack may be balanced both ways

questions.text: What is written about the one who gathered much and the one who gathered little?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 quotes: He who gathered much had nothing left over, and he who gathered little had no lack.

answers.text: He who gathered much had nothing left over, and he who gathered little had no lack
He who gathered much was blessed, and he who gathered little was shamed
He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly in the end
He has scattered abroad, he has given to the poor

questions.text: How is the brother sent together with Titus described in verse 18?
questions.explanation: Verse 18 describes him as the brother whose praise in the Good News is known throughout all the assemblies.

answers.text: As the first fruits of Achaia among all of the brothers
As a partner in the service to the saints in Jerusalem
As the brother whose praise in the Good News is known throughout all the assemblies
As one appointed to stay behind in Macedonia for a while
